verses.verse:
अनुध्याय स्वरान् सर्वान् विधिना वादयेन्मुहुः।
गतिं न्यूनाधिकमं कूर्याद् यथाशक्ति शनैः शनैः।९५।
verses.text: Keeping all the notes in mind, one should play them properly again and again; one should make the speed less or more, gradually, according to one's strength.

commentary.text: While doing the ārohāvaroha (ascent and descent) of the notes, the player should also keep in mind the names of those notes, so that, if asked suddenly, he can quickly play any note and show it. Just as children learning multiplication tables want to repeat from the beginning to answer any question, the same thing happens to those practitioners.
The second suggestion is that if, while playing the ārohāvaroha (ascent and descent), its speed increases, let it increase only so far that the purity of the notes is not spoiled.
The third suggestion is that, while increasing the speed, when some errors appear, correct them at that same speed; then, when you feel unable, reduce that speed little by little.

The fourth point is this: if you take the form of ārohāvaroha (ascent and descent) made in this order — (Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni Ṡa Ṙe Ṡa Ni Dha Pa Ma Ga Re Sa) (ṭa ka ṭa ka ṭa ka ṭa ka ṭa ka ṭa ka ka ṭa ṭa ka) — as a great mantra, and chant it attentively at least a hundred times with mental counting, then along with the fingers, the tongue and the breath, the mind too is trained, and through this practice many kinds of siddhis (accomplishments) are attained. The practitioner can see this for himself through his faith; this secret is not fit to be written.
Now the method of practising the notes with tāla (metric cycle) is presented.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
